title: Project and Supply Chain Management, B.S. (Behrend)
notes: Pattern B by definition, and NOT the same program as University Park's Backend/degree_plans/SCM-2026.json ('Supply Chain and Information Systems, B.S.', Smeal College of Business) -- different official title, different department (Behrend's own Black School of Business vs. Smeal), and a genuinely different required-course list: this major centers on project management (MGMT 418, MGMT 410, PMP-adjacent coursework) alongside supply chain, which Smeal's UP program does not require at all. Real prereq chains verified directly against Backend/catalogs/*.json before scheduling: ACCTG 211, STAT 200, and SCM 200 each require MATH 21 (which has no prereq of its own and isn't otherwise on this major's list, so it's scheduled explicitly in Semester 1 -- same MATH-chain-completion convention used for Backend/degree_plans/MGMT-2026.json and BUSINESS-2026.json); SCM 301 requires ACCTG 211 AND ECON 102 AND (SCM 200 or STAT 200); MGMT 410, MGMT 415, and MGMT 418 all require SCM 301 AND (MGMT 410 itself, once completed, satisfies the second half of 415/418's own AND-group) -- so MGMT 410 is scheduled before both, matching real prereq order rather than the bulletin's own suggested plan, which shows MGMT 410 and 'MGMT/SCM 415' in the same nominal term (not achievable given the real prereq, so this plan reorders 415 to the following semester instead of reproducing that scheduling conflict verbatim). Of the paired 'A or B' requirements, this plan picks the option with the cleaner prereq chain when both need the same underlying courses anyway: MGMT 410 over BA 421 (BA 421 needs BA 321 AND BA 322, two courses this major doesn't otherwise require), MGMT 415 over SCM 416 (SCM 416 only needs SCM 301, but MGMT 415 is already unlocked once MGMT 410 is scheduled and matches the bulletin's own suggested-plan pairing), and MGMT 471W over BA 422W/BA 462 for the Strategic Management pick (MGMT 471W needs exactly the four courses -- MGMT 301, MKTG 301, FIN 301, SCM 301 -- already required elsewhere in this plan). General Education (45cr, 21cr of which the bulletin says overlaps with the Major requirement -- not modeled as literal double-counted line items here, since this app's plan-item model has no double-counting mechanism; instead GenEd is modeled as its own generic 45cr block, consistent with every other business major already in this repo) plus the entrance-to-major courses (etm-tagged: ENGL 15/30H, MATH 110/140, ECON 102, ACCTG 211, SCM 200) round out the plan. Totals 120cr in this simulation, matching the bulletin's own stated 4-year, 121cr suggested plan almost exactly.
